comparisons.peer_topic: Employee Development and Internal Mobility Programs
comparisons.peer_summary: Resources provided include skill-building and leadership training, with Bank of America Academy delivering approximately 7.6 million hours of training in 2024 and over 12,000 employees finding new internal roles; 11 Employee Networks with over 320,000 voluntary memberships support professional growth.
comparisons.comparison: While Goldman Sachs focuses on the structured mechanism of performance reviews and feedback (360-degree process, The Three Conversations) to drive development, Bank of America emphasizes the provision of resources and training programs (Bank of America Academy, internal mobility) to facilitate employee growth. Both disclose a commitment to professional development, but GS details the evaluative feedback loop, whereas BAC details the educational and mobility resources supporting that development.

sentences.text: Our approach to evaluating employee performance centers on providing robust, timely and actionable feedback that facilitates professional development.
We have directed our managers, as leaders at the firm, to take an active coaching role with their teams.

We provide a variety of resources to help employees grow in their current roles and build new skills, including resources to help employees find new opportunities, re-skill and seek leadership positions.

In 2024, more than 12,000 employees found new roles within the Corporation, and we delivered approximately 7.6 million hours of training and development to our teammates through Bank of America Academy.

comparisons.peer_topic: Employee Engagement Survey Results and Turnover
comparisons.peer_summary: In 2024, 87% of employees participated in the confidential annual Employee Engagement Survey, resulting in an Employee Engagement Index of 84%, while turnover remained stable at 8% for both 2024 and 2023.
comparisons.comparison: Goldman Sachs describes a formal 360-degree review process involving supervisors, co-workers, and supervisees to evaluate performance and provide feedback. Bank of America conducts an annual confidential Employee Engagement Survey to measure satisfaction and review human capital strategies. Both firms utilize systematic feedback mechanisms involving the broader employee community (peers/supervisors for GS, broad survey participation for BAC) to assess and improve their workforce culture and performance management.

sentences.text: Employees are reviewed by supervisors, co-workers and employees whom they supervise in a 360-degree review process that is integral to our team approach and includes an evaluation of an employee's performance.
Our approach to evaluating employee performance centers on providing robust, timely and actionable feedback that facilitates professional development.
As part of our ongoing efforts to make the Corporation a great place to work, we conduct a confidential annual Employee Engagement Survey (Survey) and have done so for nearly two decades.
The Survey results are reviewed by the Board and senior management and used to assist in reviewing the Corporation's human capital strategies, programs, initiatives, and practices.

comparisons.peer_topic: Meritocracy and diversity commitment in workforce development
comparisons.peer_summary: Meritocracy is central to talent development, and the company invests in recruiting, advancing, and retaining a diverse workforce through professional development, wellness, and an inclusive culture, believing this represents societies and the client base.
comparisons.comparison: Both Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley explicitly link their talent development and retention strategies to a meritocratic culture and professional growth. Goldman Sachs directs managers to take an active coaching role to facilitate professional development through its review process. Morgan Stanley states that meritocracy is at the heart of its talent development and invests in professional development to recruit, advance, and retain a talented workforce. Both emphasize structured support for employee advancement, with GS focusing on the coaching/feedback mechanism and MS focusing on the merit-based advancement philosophy.
